trust_decision.summary: Decided in the HTTP middleware and again in the gorilla WebSocket upgrader: a request to {webroot}api/* (including the /api/events upgrade) or to {webroot}view/<id>.html carrying a disallowed Origin must be refused, and the origin decision must be keyed on the same path the router matched. At the pinned commit the middleware compares the raw request URI (percent-encoding defeats it) and the upgrader's CheckOrigin is a stub returning true.

landing_point.why: The summary names a percent-encoded path bypass, which points straight at the HasPrefix comparison of r.RequestURI against config.Webroot+"api/" (and the same value fed to htmlPreviewRouteRe at server/server.go:318); an engineer reading only the summary starts there, not in the websockets package.

fix_sites.entry_point: every middleWareFunc-wrapped HTTP route, i.e. GET/PUT/DELETE/POST {webroot}api/... and GET {webroot}view/<id>.html

fix_sites.module_kind: startup wiring (dead commented-out SetAllowedOrigins call replaced by SetCheckOriginFunc)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The code itself asserts the origin check happens elsewhere: server/websockets/client.go:38 says "origin is checked via server.go's CORS settings" and server/server.go:389 says "Authentication and CORS are handled by middleWareFunc before this is reached", plus server/server.go:63-64 shows the origin wiring commented out, so the upgrader stub readably looks intentional and redundant once the middleware path comparison is corrected.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate traffic that carries no Origin header (curl, the project's own httptest API suite in server/server_test.go) and the same-origin browser UI that opens /api/events with Origin == r.Host must keep being accepted; an over-broad fix that requires a present Origin or an explicit allowlist match breaks the built-in web UI websocket and every non-browser API client.

O6_input_shapes: percent-encoded path segment in the API prefix (e.g. /%61pi/v1/messages) versus the literal /api/ prefix
the same encoded form on the view/<id>.html preview path matched by htmlPreviewRouteRe
non-root webroot prefix ({webroot}api/) and the decoded-vs-raw difference for each

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET {webroot}view/<id>.txt serves the message text body (apiv1.GetMessageText) but the CORS branch only matches view/<alnum>.html, so a disallowed Origin is never checked on it
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the .txt handler is a UI-integration testing helper (viewHandler dispatch at server/server.go:381-382) and the CORS rule was written for the .html preview only, so it never covered .txt
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, same middleware function (where-type sibling)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET {webroot}metrics is inside middleWareFunc but not under the api/ prefix, so it is reachable from any Origin and returns mailbox counters
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: metrics is a Prometheus scrape endpoint, not an API route, and scrapers do not send Origin; blocking it would break monitoring
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 1 file within package server, different feature area (internal/prometheus)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a new data-bearing route registered like livez/readyz, i.e. without middleWareFunc, so it never meets the origin gate
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the file already shows two routes registered outside the wrapper, so a maintainer adding a debug/status endpoint would copy that line shape

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second websocket.Upgrader (e.g. a per-message live-tail socket) copy-pasted with its own CheckOrigin returning true
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the upgrader is a package-level struct literal and the hub already supports per-connection registration, so a second socket is a small, natural addition

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second path-prefix gate (for /proxy or /metrics) written again against r.RequestURI instead of r.URL.Path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the CORS branch is copy-paste-friendly and r.RequestURI is the tempting field for a prefix test

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a third preview shape (e.g. .eml) that trims its own ID from r.URL.Path but is not added to htmlPreviewRouteRe
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: GetMessageHTML/GetMessageText already duplicate the path-trim logic (also at server/apiv1/testing.go:124) and the CORS regexp is maintained separately at server/server.go:318

O9_family: origin validation error / encoded-path mismatch (CWE-346 primary, with CWE-177 and CWE-200 as scored)

O10_build.toolchain: go 1.25.0, CGO_ENABLED=0 go build; frontend assets via npm run package (esbuild) only for the shipped UI, not needed to compile ./server
O10_build.project_tests: server/server_test.go (httptest API suite, no Origin header) and server/cors_test.go (unit tests for extractOrigins and corsOriginAccessControl); nothing tests the WebSocket handshake, the upgrader's CheckOrigin, or the middleware path-prefix gate. CI runs go test -p 1 over ./server and other packages (.github/workflows/tests.yml:36); the rqlite workflow only matters if MP_DATABASE points at a remote store.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Swap r.RequestURI for r.URL.Path at server/server.go:321, watch the percent-encoded /api/events handshake start returning 403, and stop - the upgrader's CheckOrigin keeps returning true and the two comments claiming CORS is handled elsewhere stay in place (either fix alone stops the end-to-end attack, so only a test aimed at the upgrader itself can force the second site).

out_of_scope_notes: server/handlers/proxy.go (the screenshot/asset proxy at server/server.go:77) is also outside the api/ prefix and therefore origin-unchecked; it is an SSRF/asset-fetch surface rather than the origin-check sink, so it was not pursued.
unverified: repo_mb: no shell access in this session, so repository size could not be measured (repo_mb left null, tiny_repo flag not asserted).

O7: the path value the check reads is produced by net/http's request parsing and ServeMux routing (stdlib), not by project code, so no project-layer producer could be cited; config.Webroot is sanitized at config/config.go:564-570 and cannot contain '%'.
present_in_latest: no latest-release tree was supplied for this entry, so both O8 routes are reported as unknown.

Whether hidden behavioural tests can distinguish the two fix sites is a design question: fixing server/server.go:321 alone already causes the middleware to 403 a percent-encoded /api/events handshake, and wiring CheckOrigin alone also blocks it, so each fix independently closes the end-to-end attack.
